subject: She Left, and I Let Her
message:
Dear Reader,

Liza left. Quietly, without a word. She placed money on the table for me... out of pity.

Do you understand what that means? I made her believe in me, then broke her. And in the end, she still pitied me.

There are things too shameful for even the Underground to confess.

I didn't go after her.

Regards,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: I Tried to Break Her
message:
Dear Reader,

I told her love is a lie. That she'd end up in filth and ruin. That men like me can only destroy.

Her eyes... she didn't cry. She just looked. Through me.

And suddenly I felt—small. Contemptible.

Why did I bring her here? To punish her? Or myself?

Yours in shame,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: She Came to See Me
message:
Dear Reader,

She came. Liza. The girl from the brothel. She remembered the address I scribbled in a moment of derangement.

I panicked. My room, my life—filthy. I am not the man I pretended to be that night.

I shouted. Mocked her. Tried to push her away.

But she stayed. She wanted to understand me.

In distress,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: I Gave Her My Address
message:
Dear Reader,

After I spoke of mothers and graves and warmth long lost, I felt something melt in her eyes.

I gave her my address. Why? I don't even know. Maybe I wanted to be found.

Maybe I wanted someone to look behind the wall.

Until then,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: On the Nature of Prostitutes and Salvation
message:
Dear Reader,

I told her she was lost. I painted her future—illness, poverty, an unmarked grave. I tried to scare her, to awaken something.

But when I spoke of mothers and hope, she... listened.

I don't know what I'm doing. I am not a savior.

But for a moment, I believed I could be.

Strangely,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: Liza, the Girl at the Brothel
message:
Dear Reader,

I found myself at the brothel. I spoke to a girl named Liza.

She was quiet. Broken, perhaps. I began to preach, to moralize—to rescue her.

But who was I to speak of dignity, of salvation?

Am I not the most fallen of all?

Conflicted,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: The Officer - A Petty Victory
message:
Dear Reader,

For years, I imagined revenge against the officer who once moved me aside like a speck.

Today, I walked directly into him. Shoulder to shoulder.

He did not notice.

And yet I felt victorious. Is this all I have left?

Sincerely,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: I Crashed the Dinner
message:
Dear Reader,

I forced my way into Zverkov's dinner. I was not wanted.

I humiliated myself. I insulted them. I begged for attention. They ignored me, then mocked me.

So I challenged Zverkov to a duel.

They laughed.

Yes, I am aware. Pathetic.

With resentment,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: They Left Without Me
message:
Dear Reader,

They planned a farewell dinner for Zverkov. I was invited out of obligation.

I arrived late. Intentionally. I wanted them to wait for me.

They didn't.

I chased them to the restaurant. I think I hate them. I think I hate myself more.

In bitterness,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: A Dinner Invitation, or a Trap?
message:
Dear Reader,

Simonov invited me to a dinner. Zverkov will be there. Zverkov—the man they all adore, the man I despise.

I said yes. Why?

Maybe I want to be seen. Maybe I want to sabotage myself.

Maybe that's all I've ever done.

Contemplatively,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: I Dressed Like a Gentleman
message:
Dear Reader,

I prepared for the dinner. Dressed up. Cleaned my boots. Practiced how I would speak.

For whom? For people I detest.

I think I wanted to be better than them. But already I feel like a fool.

In discomfort,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: Imaginary Duels and Old Debts
message:
Dear Reader,

Before the dinner, I imagined conversations. Conflicts. Witty retorts.

But what can I say to them? I owe Simonov money. I am nothing to them.

I will go anyway. Perhaps I'll say nothing at all.

Defiantly,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: My Former Schoolmates
message:
Dear Reader,

I saw them again. Ferfichkin, Trudolyubov, Simonov... and Zverkov.

I remember how they used to look at me. Not with hatred—worse. With indifference.

I never forgave them for that.

Still haven't.

Sincerely,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: The Joy of Being Insulted
message:
Dear Reader,

There's a peculiar pleasure in being insulted. Especially when one deserves it.

But I never respond. Never lash out. I just... watch. Quietly.

They think that means they've won.

Let them.

In silence,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: I Write, Therefore I Am
message:
Dear Reader,

Why write these things? For you? No.

I write because I am rotting. Because this is all I have left. Memory, bitterness, observation.

Maybe someday someone will read this and understand me.

Or hate me. That would be something too.

Yours,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: On Men of Action
message:
Dear Reader,

They act. They do things. Build bridges, conquer lands, marry, fight.

They never ask why. Never hesitate.

Fools.

I admire them. I envy them. I despise them.

Because I cannot act.

In paralysis,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: Even If I Had a Reason
message:
Dear Reader,

Some say reason guides man.

They lie. A man acts out of spite, contradiction, chaos.

He does what he knows will ruin him—because it ruins him.

Man is not piano keys. He is illness.

We are not civilized. We are clever brutes.

In madness,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: The Curse of Too Much Consciousness
message:
Dear Reader,

To be too aware is to rot from the inside out.

Give me ignorance. Simplicity. The blindness of a peasant.

But I see too much. I feel too deeply.

I drown in details.

With tired eyes,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: Why I Refuse to Be Cured
message:
Dear Reader,

I do not want to be cured. I cling to my sickness like a child to a blanket.

Let the world function without me.

I am comfortable in my darkness.

With affection for decay,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: I Am a Sick Man - An Underground Introduction
message:
Dear Reader,

I am a sick man... I am a spiteful man. I believe my liver is diseased. But I know nothing at all about my disease, and I don't consult a doctor. Out of spite, perhaps.

Do I believe in medicine? No. I respect only facts, and I find them loathsome.

But what can a man write who is tormented by consciousness? A man who sees too clearly, who cannot even become anything—not even an insect.

Welcome to my underground.

Yours in bitterness,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: The Inertia of Underground Living
message:
Dear Reader,

To live underground is not simply to be hidden.

It is to exist in hesitation. To overthink every step until the step vanishes.

In the end, I do nothing. And I find comfort in that.

From the void,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: The Piano Keys Illusion
message:
Dear Reader,

They say man is a machine. That he presses a key, and out comes an emotion.

But I tell you: man will press the wrong key just to prove he is free.

He will bleed for his right to be unreasonable.

That is what separates us from arithmetic.

In resistance,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: What If 2 + 2 = 5?
message:
Dear Reader,

Reason says 2 + 2 = 4.

But what if a man insists it equals 5?

Is he mad? Or simply free?

Freedom is not in truth. It is in the ability to defy truth.

I choose 5.

Deliriously,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: The Wall
message:
Dear Reader,

We all hit a wall. The unchangeable. The immutable. And what do we do?

We lie to ourselves that the wall doesn't exist. Or we bash our heads against it out of spite.

That is the only freedom left.

Yours rebelliously,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: Pleasure in Toothaches
message:
Dear Reader,

You think I jest. But there is genuine pleasure in suffering. Even in a toothache.

We moan, we whimper—not just from pain, but from the joy of hearing ourselves suffer.

We want an audience. Even if it's just the mirror.

In perverse delight,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: Why I Didn't See a Doctor
message:
Dear Reader,

My liver is failing. My body is failing. But I will not go to a doctor.

What would be the point? So they can tell me what I already know?

To rebel against reason is a sweet, stupid joy.

In spite,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: Why I Write
message:
Dear Reader,

I write for no one. I publish nothing. I write only to exist—to prove I have existed.

Each word is a shadow. Each sentence, a whisper from the cellar.

You are not here. Yet I speak.

To no one,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: A Life in a Cellar
message:
Dear Reader,

For years I have lived like this. Alone. Thinking. Watching.

It is not a home. It is a burrow. A grave before death.

But it is mine.

Buried,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: I Am Not Even an Insect
message:
Dear Reader,

I could not become wicked. Nor good. Nor anything.

There were moments I wanted to be vile—but couldn't.

Even cockroaches have purpose. I envy them.

Without form,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: Forty Years Old and Still Underground
message:
Dear Reader,

I'm over forty. Alone. A retired civil servant. I once held a post—small, unnecessary.

I was rude, petty, forgotten.

Now I am nothing at all.

Still writing,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: The Office Clerk I Once Was
message:
Dear Reader,

I used to work in an office. I was polite—then insolent. I despised my superiors, yet feared them.

I made copies of meaningless documents and believed myself superior to the world.

Such are the delusions of small men.

In reflection,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: Why I Insulted Petitioners
message:
Dear Reader,

People used to visit my desk for signatures. I looked at them with disdain. I delayed them, mocked them silently.

I hated their faces—their normalcy.

Yet I envied it too.

Pettily yours,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: I Dreamed of Greatness
message:
Dear Reader,

I wanted to be Napoleon once.

Yes, me. The man who hides from his landlord.

Ambition is a disease. It burns through nobodies like fever.

I burned out long ago.

In mockery of myself,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: I Watched My Landlord
message:
Dear Reader,

I peek through the door when he visits. He knows I'm there. We both pretend otherwise.

He represents the surface world—simple, functional, dull.

And I, the rot beneath it.

Underground still,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: When They Laughed at Me
message:
Dear Reader,

At the office, they once laughed at me for wearing an old coat. I smiled, as if it did not hurt.

It did.

I plotted imaginary revenge for weeks. But did nothing.

In silent fury,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: The Nature of Ridicule
message:
Dear Reader,

There are few tortures more exquisite than being ridiculous and knowing it.

We sense others' laughter long before they utter it.

Consciousness magnifies every smirk.

I wish I were a fool.

Yours lucidly,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: The Dinner I Couldn't Attend
message:
Dear Reader,

They invited me to dinners before, and I never went. Always imagined myself arriving triumphantly, admired, envied.

In truth, I feared being seen.

There is power in absence.

Humbly absent,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: Men Like Me Shouldn't Exist
message:
Dear Reader,

Perhaps I shouldn't have been born. Men like me—half-thinking, half-feeling—serve no one.

We analyze until the moment passes. We rot in possibilities.

Maybe oblivion is mercy.

From nowhere,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: Freedom Through Suffering
message:
Dear Reader,

There is a kind of freedom that only suffering provides. It strips away all illusions.

Once you have nothing left, no expectations remain.

That is peace.

In bleakness,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: Why I Live Underground
message:
Dear Reader,

Why live like this? Because it is safer below. The air may be stale, but it is mine.

Up there, one must perform. Down here, I simply am.

Hidden,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: Consciousness Is a Curse
message:
Dear Reader,

To think too much is to destroy yourself. Thought eats the heart, one idea at a time.

Animals live without reflection. They are blessed.

We reflect, and rot.

In awareness,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: When I Tried to Pray
message:
Dear Reader,

I once tried to pray, but it felt dishonest. Even before God, I was acting.

Everything I do is performance. Even this confession.

Is there truth left in me?

Hopelessly,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: The Mouse and the Man
message:
Dear Reader,

A mouse retreats to its hole when struck—it whimpers but still defends its little dignity.

Man, however, knows he is beaten and invents philosophy to justify his cowardice.

I am that man.

Self-aware and useless,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: A Formula for Humanity
message:
Dear Reader,

They seek formulas for happiness, for behavior, for society.

But I ask: what happens when man grows bored of perfection?

He will smash it, just to feel alive again.

Perfection is unbearable.

Yours in rebellion,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: Useless Thoughts Before Sleep
message:
Dear Reader,

I think before sleeping, then think about the thinking, and so on until morning.

One must live somehow, even if only in ideas.

And yet, ideas never keep you warm.

Restlessly,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: I Once Loved a Dream
message:
Dear Reader,

I once loved an idea of love. Pure, distant, unreal.

Real affection terrifies me—it smells of sweat and compromise.

Dreams, however, never touch you back.

Dreaming still,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: Even Rats Need Warmth
message:
Dear Reader,

I mock people who seek love, yet I crave it too.

We all do. Even rats huddle for warmth.

I am alone, but not immune to the cold.

From the cellar,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: The Mathematical Men
message:
Dear Reader,

They wish to turn man into an equation—predictable, logical, precise.

But man will never be an equation. He will add error out of boredom.

Without error, there is no soul.

Incorrectly yours,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: An Apology, or Perhaps a Confession
message:
Dear Reader,

Do not think I write to justify myself. I know what I am.

But perhaps in confessing, one cleans the wound slightly.

Or only deepens it.

Bleeding still,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com

subject: Farewell from the Underground
message:
Dear Reader,

There will be no more letters.

Words cannot save me. They only echo louder in this damp room.

Do not look for me. There is nothing to find.

In final solitude,
The Underground Man

The Underground Man
Unemployed Thinker, St. Petersburg Basement
fjodor@dostoyevsky.com
